newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices surge on cold forecast.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices surge on cold forecast.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices rallied Wednesday on the heels of a significant cold front throughout the eastern two-thirds of the U.S., causing some companies to limit deliverability, market sources said.

Gulf Coast prices jumped into the $4.20s and $4.30s per mmBtu, up more than 20 cents from Tuesday, as the Northeast and Gulf areas awaited the return of cold temperatures Thursday through early next week.
A significant drawdown in storage expected in AGA's report also sent buyers to the spot market in droves. A Reuter poll showed most expectations between 110 and 120 bcf.

Further east, where storage levels were about 20 percent ahead of year-ago, New York city-gate prices regained their lead on indices by rising to a high of $5.25. Traders said most deals were done in the low-$5 area for Thursday delivery.
Weather Services Corp said much colder temperatures will likely arrive to the Northeast by Friday, carrying some precipitation.
Below-normal temperatures are expected to continue in the area through next week.

In the Midcontinent, where temperatures are expected to drop to about 10 degrees below normal Thursday and then even lower Friday, prices surged an average of 80 cents to the $5.05-5.10 range. Deals were reported done anywhere from $4.60 to $5.50.
In response to the critical days declared by Northern Illinois Gas, Peoples Gas and NGPL for Thursday, Chicago city-gate prices soared to as high as $6.75 before settling back into the $5 area.
As a result of the critical day, the Midwest utilities will limit storage withdrawals and deliveries from their Illinois facilities.
In west Texas, Permian gas prices were also about 80 cents higher around $5, with deals reported done anywhere from $4.80 to $5.25.
Similarly at Waha, prices jumped into the low-$5 area, as Texas awaited the arrival of much colder weather Thursday and the Midwest demanded large volumes of gas.
In south Texas, prices ranged from $4.25 to as high as $5 at the Houston Ship Channel. Traders said most deals were done in the low-$4.50s.
